complaint: The attic motion detector misses events; its battery warning appeared today. But it also missed an event last week, well before the warning, so I'm not sure the battery is the cause. It was boiling up there all summer, so maybe the heat damaged it. Should I replace the whole sensor?
usability_reason: The response is polite and includes actionable follow-up steps (confirm online status, test motion, monitor 24 hours). However, it claims the battery was low at 8% and that this caused the sensor to go offline, neither of which appears in the session record; the record only shows a battery replacement and successful test. It also closes the case as resolved with root cause BATTERY_LOW despite the customer's reasonable concern that an earlier missed event predated the warning, and it does not address the heat-damage question or whether to replace the whole sensor. Clarity is adequate but the unsupported claims and premature closure reduce usability.
